design.text: Multi-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; patients randomized 2:1 to a single 2 gram oral dose of SYM-1219 versus placebo, self-administered on Day 1.

citations.quote: Trial SYM-1219-301 was a phase 3, multi-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of SYM-1219 2 Grams for the treatment of women and postmenarchal adolescent girls with bacterial vaginosis.

Randomization: Patients determined to be eligible at the Baseline visit (Study Day 1) were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive a single dose of 2 gms of SYM-1219 and placebo to be self-administered on Day 1 (without regard to meals).

population.text: Non-pregnant adult females and postmenarchal adolescent girls (aged 18 to 54 years) with bacterial vaginosis.

citations.quote: Trial 1 enrolled 144 non-pregnant female patients aged 19 to 54 years and Trial 2 enrolled 189 non-pregnant females aged 18 to 54 years.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint was Clinical Outcome (Clinical Responder) evaluated at the TOC/EOS visit (Day 21 to 30): normal vaginal discharge, negative 10% KOH Whiff test, and clue cells less than 20% of total epithelial cells.

citations.quote: The primary endpoint was Clinical Outcome evaluated at the TOC/EOS visit (Day 21 to 30). A Clinical Outcome Responder was defined as a patient with all of the following:

- Normal vaginal discharge
- Negative 10% KOH Whiff test
- Clue cells less than 20% of the total epithelial cells on microscopic examination of the vaginal wet mount using saline.

n.text: 189 patients enrolled; primary analysis mITT population N=164 (SYM-1219 2 g N=107, placebo N=57).

citations.quote: Number of patients: A total of 189 patients were enrolled.

A total of 189 subjects were randomized in the trial SYM 1219-301. There were 189 subjects in the safety population as well. The primary analysis population which was the mITT population had a total of 164 subjects.

result.text: Clinical Responder rate at Day 21-30 was 53.3% with SOLOSEC vs 19.3% with placebo (difference 34.0; 95% CI 18.7, 49.3; p<0.001). Therapeutic Responder rate was 34.6% vs 3.5% (p<0.001).

citations.quote: In the mITT population, the Therapeutic Outcome Responder Rate in the secnidazole 2 gram treatment group was statistically superior to placebo (p<0.001) at the TOC/EOS and Interim visit. About 34.6% of subjects (37/107) in the secnidazole 2 gm arm were therapeutic responders at end of treatment and at interim visit compared to 3.5%(2/57) in the placebo arm.

indication.text: SOLOSEC is a nitroimidazole antimicrobial indicated for the treatment of bacterial vaginosis in adult women.

target_moa.text: Secnidazole is a 5-nitroimidazole antimicrobial; it enters the bacterial cell as an inactive prodrug where the nitro group is reduced by bacterial enzymes to radical anions that interfere with bacterial DNA synthesis of susceptible isolates.

citations.quote: Secnidazole is a 5-nitroimidazole antimicrobial. 5-nitroimidazoles enter the bacterial cell as an inactive prodrug where the nitro group is reduced by bacterial enzymes to radical anions. It is believed that these radical anions interfere with bacterial DNA synthesis of susceptible isolates.

SYM-1219 (secnidazole) is an oral, antimicrobial drug in the 5-nitroimidazole class representing a new chemical entity (NCE) in the United States (US), for the treatment of women with Bacterial Vaginosis (BV).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=2%) were vulvo-vaginal candidiasis, headache, nausea, dysgeusia, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and vulvovaginal pruritus. In placebo-controlled trials, vulvo-vaginal candidiasis occurred in 9.6% (SOLOSEC N=197) vs 2.9% (placebo N=136); headache 3.6% vs 1.5%; nausea 3.6% vs 0.7%. No deaths occurred.
